clue.text: Sauce-boat at University?

parts.note: a ketch is a two-masted sailing boat
to be up is to be in residence at a university, especially Oxford or Cambridge

explanation.surface: A gravy boat on a college high table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sauce-boat' reads as one thing, a gravy jug, but the hyphen splits the definition from the boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Tomato condiment poured over chips is a kind of sauce.

clue.text: Frolicsome friends wrap up half-hearted game

indicators.note: wrap up means the word for friends goes around the game

parts.note: kith are friends, as in kith and kin

indicators.note: half-hearted means one of the two middle letters of the game is dropped

explanation.surface: Playful companions finish off a lacklustre match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-hearted' drops one N from the heart of TENNIS, leaving TENIS, which 'wrap up' puts inside KITH.
explanation.definitionFit: Playful and lively, like a young cat.

clue.text: Sad, his being excluded from this rebuke

indicators.note: being excluded from means these letters are taken out of what follows

explanation.surface: Someone is upset at being left out of a telling-off.
explanation.walkthrough: THIS plus EARFUL gives THISEARFUL; 'being excluded from' removes HIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Crying, on the verge of tears, unhappy.

clue.text: Game to dance and drink

parts.note: a hop is an informal dance

explanation.surface: Playing a game of dancing and drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: A children's playground game of hopping through chalked squares.

clue.text: Get through a critical situation

explanation.surface: Survive a crisis.
explanation.definitionFit: Succeed in an exam; and a crisis point, as in 'come to a pretty pass'.

clue.text: Fan's expression of opinion when dumped in river

definitions.note: the definition is 'fan', with the 's standing for 'is'

indicators.note: something dumped in a river is put inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Wales, Scotland and England
casting a vote expresses an opinion

explanation.surface: A supporter's view that a team or player has been thrown into the river.
explanation.definitionFit: An ardent enthusiast or follower is a fan.

clue.text: Device at TA manoeuvres to render harmless

indicators.note: manoeuvres suggests moving things about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The Territorial Army practises defusing a bomb.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's reserve force, which fits the military surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To make a device or bomb inoperative and safe.

clue.text: Legitimate to support state with capital cover

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits beneath, so it comes after

parts.note: a lid covers the head, the capital

explanation.surface: It is lawful to back the state with funds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like money but means head, which a lid covers.
explanation.definitionFit: Lawful, sound, legally acceptable.

clue.text: Blunder over oil pollution in Libya

indicators.note: in a down clue over means the first piece sits above the next

parts.note: a trip is a slip or blunder

indicators.note: pollution suggests the oil is spoiled, so its letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A mistake leads to an oil spill in Libya.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pollution' turns OIL into OLI. The definition is the capital city found in Libya.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital city of Libya, on its Mediterranean coast.

clue.text: In French art, the priest is for the stake

indicators.note: In means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: VEN, Venerable, title of an archdeacon

explanation.surface: In French painting, the priest is burned at the stake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'art' is the old verb form, 'thou art', not painting.
explanation.definitionFit: Betting odds of one to one, winning an amount equal to the stake.

clue.text: Down-and-out's cunning rebuffed by politician

definitions.note: the definition is 'down-and-out', with the 's standing for 'is'

indicators.note: rebuffed suggests being pushed back, so the word for cunning is read backwards

parts.note: art can mean craft or cunning

explanation.surface: A homeless person's guile meets with rejection from an MP.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rebuffed' turns ART into TRA.
explanation.definitionFit: A vagrant with no home is a destitute wanderer.

clue.text: Minor Warrant Officer hitherto unsurpassed

parts.note: a sergeant major, SM, is a warrant officer in the British Army
an all-time record has never been bettered

explanation.surface: A junior warrant officer whose record has never been beaten.
explanation.definitionFit: Petty or unimportant, operating on a small scale.

clue.text: Rub out four different notes

parts.note: E, F, A and C are musical notes; spelling the answer uses only these four different ones

explanation.surface: Erase four wrong notes from a score.
explanation.walkthrough: Six letters but only four different notes: E, F, A and C, with E and F each used twice.
explanation.definitionFit: To erase or obliterate something is to efface it from view.

clue.text: Academic has work-rooms outside the University

indicators.note: outside means the word for work-rooms wraps around the other piece

parts.note: studios are rooms where artists work

explanation.surface: A don whose workshops lie off the campus.
explanation.definitionFit: Given to scholarly reading and diligent learning.

clue.text: Devilish hopes, to rid Henry II of one of its members!

definitions.text: Devilish hopes, to rid Henry II of one of its members!

indicators.note: devilish suggests mischief, so these letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Henry II's wicked wish to be rid of a troublesome cleric.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry II reputedly asked to be rid of a turbulent priest, Thomas Becket, who was then murdered.
explanation.definitionFit: The body of clergy, of which Becket was one.

clue.text: Man is too big to be described as one

definitions.text: Man is too big to be described as one

parts.words: Man is too big to be described as one
parts.note: the Isle of Man is a sizeable island, too large to be called a little one

explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' looks like a person but is the Isle of Man, a self-governing island in the Irish Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny island, smaller than the Isle of Man.

clue.text: Loathsome as peasants were in 1381

explanation.surface: Rebellious medieval serfs were thoroughly disgusting.
explanation.walkthrough: The Peasants' Revolt of 1381 was an English uprising against the poll tax.
explanation.definitionFit: Repulsive or disgusting; and rising up in rebellion against authority.

clue.text: Remarkable motto written above some lines

indicators.note: in a down clue, written above means the first piece sits on top of the rest

parts.note: a legend is an inscription or motto
a, as in some or one

explanation.surface: A motto inscribed over a few lines of text.
explanation.definitionFit: Famous, celebrated, the stuff of stories.

clue.text: Development of joke relating to a continent, say

indicators.note: say signals that the words are heard, not written

parts.note: a jest is a joke, and Asian relates to a continent

explanation.surface: How a joke about Asia evolves.
explanation.definitionFit: The growth of a foetus in the womb, or of an idea.

clue.text: Aperture intended, say, for a tablet

parts.note: a hatch is an opening in a floor, wall or deck

indicators.note: say signals that the word for intended is heard, not written

explanation.surface: A gap meant to hold a commemorative plaque.
explanation.definitionFit: A diamond-shaped board bearing a dead person's coat of arms, hung as a memorial.

clue.text: Popular leader endlessly attempted to import food

indicators.note: to import means bring something inside, so one piece goes in the other
endlessly means the last letter is cut off

explanation.surface: A populist who kept trying to bring in groceries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts TRIED to TRIE, and 'to import' puts BUN inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: In ancient Rome, an official elected to protect the plebs, a champion of the people.

clue.text: Marijuana? Tell the cops

explanation.surface: Someone caught with cannabis decides to inform the police.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang a grass is a police informer, and to grass is to inform on someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for cannabis; and slang for informing on criminals to police.

clue.text: Do away with a vessel out west -his, possibly

indicators.note: out means the letter for west is removed
possibly means the letters can be rearranged

explanation.surface: Get rid of a dish heading out west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' removes W from BOWL, giving BOL; 'possibly' rearranges HIS into ISH.
explanation.definitionFit: To end or put an end to a law or practice.

clue.text: He half follows this map, perhaps, being at sea

definitions.text: He half follows this map, perhaps, being at sea

indicators.note: follows means the half-word comes after the jumble
at sea means confused or all over the place, so these letters are jumbled
half of the two-letter word is taken, its second letter

explanation.surface: A sailor follows a chart while out on the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' scrambles THIS MAP into SHIPMAT, and 'half' of HE gives E at the end. The whole clue also describes a fellow sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: A fellow sailor serving on the same vessel, out on the ocean.

clue.text: Plant in South Africa is beginning to languish

indicators.note: in means one piece sits inside the other
beginning to means only the first letter is taken

explanation.surface: A plant in South Africa starts to wilt.
explanation.definitionFit: An agave grown for its tough fibre, used in rope.

clue.text: Ancient country's channels of information

explanation.surface: An old kingdom's lines of communication.
explanation.walkthrough: Media was an ancient kingdom in what is now Iran.
explanation.definitionFit: Old kingdom of the Medes; and press, radio and television.

clue.text: The Turkish capital once produced cloth

explanation.surface: Ankara in former times made fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: Ankara, Turkey's capital, was formerly known as Angora; angora is also a soft woollen fabric from goat or rabbit hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Old name of Ankara; and fabric woven from mohair or rabbit fur.

clue.text: The way silver attracts a speculator

explanation.surface: How silver draws an investor.
explanation.walkthrough: A stag buys new shares hoping to sell at a quick profit.
explanation.definitionFit: A stock-market investor who buys new share issues for quick resale.

clue.text: Financially secure appointment in violin-making?

parts.note: a sound business is solvent and secure
a post is a job or appointment

explanation.surface: A steady, well-paid job in a luthier's workshop.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is by example: a small dowel inside a violin found in violin-making.
explanation.definitionFit: A small wooden peg wedged inside a violin's body to carry vibration.

clue.text: A politician I excuse

explanation.surface: A politician offers a personal excuse.
explanation.definitionFit: A plea that one was elsewhere, used as an excuse.

clue.text: Fish returning to protection on the sheltered side

indicators.note: returning means the word for fish is read backwards

parts.note: a ward is someone or something under protection

explanation.surface: A fish swimming back to safe water out of the wind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns EEL into LEE.
explanation.definitionFit: Downwind, away from the wind, on the protected side.

clue.text: Fabulous creature makes some angry phone calls

indicators.note: some means only part of these words is used

explanation.surface: A mythical beast keeps making irate telephone calls.
explanation.definitionFit: A mythical beast with eagle's head and lion's body, a griffin.
